posts.subject: TTT Rule
posts.bodyHtml:
Hello, this is a small thread just to point out one thing. Today I was playing on TTT and I got proven Innocent by detective (not gonna say name) and he didn't announce me as Inno, so I asked him to do it and he said that he doesn't want to. So I opened rules and realized that in Detective rules or anywhere else when I think about it, there is no such rule as "detective has to announce that he proved somebody Innocent". Yes I know that this is a small thing, but I thing this should be added to rules to inform players completely. Somebody could abuse this and somebody could do it by accident cause he/she wouldn't know that it has to be done.


Please consider it higher admins.


Thanks.

Well as far as I know, a detective not announcing innocent name after proving them could be considered as game breaking in my opinion so it could be punishable by the admins.


However, same as you, I would like to know the opinion about that.

Hey @Thorin Pikachu


not looking forward to give a long post 'bout that topic.
I'm totally the same opinion as @Luckiris
Yes but my point is that it should be added to rules to let players know, so they DONT have to be punished by admins.

Ehm,
Its the choice of the detective. He doesnt have to say that you are prooven. Nobody cares who is proofen. They dont care about it. You can say 5 times "Thorin is innocent" 1 minute later somebody will ask "is thorin proofen?" And what does it change? When the detective doesnt kill you, youre probaly innocent. Or maybe he missed his Taser.
In my opinion, it doesnt make any difference. Its only a new rule that make our Rules bigger then it has to be. The Leadership told me, that they will only add important rules / gamechanging rules. Like Camping under 1:00 is forbidden.
I think this rule is useless. The players dont even care about the Detective, or who is proofen or not. They just dont care!!

I will have to agree with @Unicorn24, I don't even say it all the time who i proved and who is innocent, I only say it if anyone asks, and I don't want to limit our players with useless rules, i like it how it's right now and I have never saw a problem with that

Not announcing someone as innocent and keeping it quiet after proving them could be used to your advantage as a detective.


Example:


Only 2 "Innos" are left, the one you proved to be innocent and the guy leftover who is the traitor.
In this situation the one as traitor be like: "It could be me, but it could also be him", BUT you know who it is.
The traitor will feel less safe, when knowing that the last guy is proven, so by proving the second guy, but not telling anyone you have the high-ground.


I know, the given example is highly unlikely to play out that exact way, but it's still something I have seen work.

As stated by @Unicorn24 people will ask a minute later who is proofed after you call a guy inno about 5 times...



They only care about " KOS "
